title: Not Only Social Networks: Channels of Dissemination of Fake News in the Views of the Population
screen_reason: Mass quota survey of 1,000 residents of the Republic of Mordovia (Russia), April-May 2023, reporting quantitative shares of respondents who self-report encountering fake news (51% at least several times a month; frequency table), who self-report having shared fake news in the past year (23%), and who name each channel as where they most often encountered fake news (social networks 58%, etc.). These are RECALL exposure and RECALL sharing shares with a stated denominator, so the paper is eligible.

estimates.measure_type: % of respondents who encountered fake news at least several times a month
estimates.value_raw: 51 % (Каждый второй / every second) of 1,000 respondents; Table 4 components: almost daily 15, several times a week 16, several times a month 19
estimates.denominator: 1,000 residents aged 18+ of the Republic of Mordovia, Russia (quota sample across 22 municipal districts and the city of Saransk, >80 settlements)
estimates.definition: Respondent self-reported frequency of coming across made-up, fake news; numerator = the three most frequent response options combined (almost daily, several times a week, several times a month)
estimates.misinfo_def: фейковые новости как выдуманную или недостоверную информацию, преднамеренно распространяемую заинтересованными сторонами для того, чтобы ввести аудиторию в заблуждение [fake news = invented or unreliable information deliberately disseminated by interested parties in order to mislead the audience]
estimates.source_quote: Каждый второй (51 %) сталкивался с ними не менее нескольких раз в месяц, в том числе 15 % – практически ежедневно (табл. 4).
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Respondent self-report only; no external verification of what respondents counted as fake news. Question wording used the term 'выдуманные, фейковые новости' (made-up, fake news); the author states respondents discussed the topic freely and that the term did not appear to cause cognitive distortion even among the oldest respondents.
estimates.moderator_quote: Всего в исследовании приняли участие 1 000 респондентов из 22 муниципальных районов и г.о. Саранск... Выборка квотная, репрезентует структуру жителей субъекта по полу, возрасту и типу расселения [In all, 1,000 respondents from 22 municipal districts and the city of Saransk took part... The sample is a quota sample representing the structure of the region's residents by sex, age and settlement type]
estimates.notes: The paper is internally inconsistent about this headline: the Results section and Table 4 give 51% (15+16+19 = 50, so 51 is the author's stated figure, kept verbatim per R8), while the English and Russian abstracts say 'three out of ten respondents encountered fake news at least several times a month' and the Discussion says 'at least a third of respondents met them over the last month'. The Results/Table 4 figure is used here because it is the one tied to the reported distribution. Note also that 25% answered 'difficult to say', which is left inside the denominator. English translation of the source quote: 'Every second respondent (51%) came across them at least several times a month, including 15% almost daily (Table 4).'

estimates.measure_type: % of respondents who encounter fake news practically every day
estimates.denominator: 1,000 residents aged 18+ of the Republic of Mordovia, Russia (quota sample)
estimates.definition: Respondent chose the highest-frequency option ('practically every day') on the fake-news encounter frequency question
estimates.misinfo_def: выдуманная или недостоверная информация, преднамеренно распространяемая... чтобы ввести аудиторию в заблуждение [invented or unreliable information deliberately disseminated in order to mislead the audience]
estimates.page_loc: Table 4 (Частота взаимодействия с фейковыми новостями), p. 169
estimates.moderator_quote: Данные о частоте встречи с выдуманными, фейковыми новостями показывают, что они стали частью повседневной жизни респондентов [Data on the frequency of encountering made-up, fake news show that they have become part of respondents' everyday life]
estimates.notes: Stricter-threshold variant of the 51% row (same question, daily rather than monthly threshold). Source quote is the Table 4 row: 'Practically every day 15(%)'.

estimates.measure_type: % of respondents who say they shared fake news with others in the past year
estimates.value_raw: ещё четверть (23 %) делились подобного рода информацией [another quarter (23%) shared this kind of information]
estimates.denominator: 1,000 residents aged 18+ of the Republic of Mordovia, Russia (quota sample)
estimates.definition: Respondent reported having passed on / shared made-up, fake information with people around them over the past year (self-reported, unintentional sharing included)
estimates.misinfo_def: выдуманная или недостоверная информация, преднамеренно распространяемая... чтобы ввести аудиторию в заблуждение [invented or unreliable information deliberately disseminated in order to mislead the audience]
estimates.source_quote: каждый третий опрошенный (32 %) за последний год верил фейкам, а ещё четверть (23 %) делились подобного рода информацией.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Respondent self-report; the author explicitly flags these as lower bounds because the questions are sensitive and because respondents may not know they were misled or misled others
estimates.moderator_quote: При этом мы имеем дело с нижними порогами [At the same time we are dealing with lower bounds]
estimates.notes: The companion 32% figure in the same sentence is BELIEF in fakes and is excluded by the protocol. The abstract renders this row as 'two out of ten shared it with others' and the Discussion as 'another quarter'; 23% is the verbatim Results figure. Source quote is de-hyphenated across a line break in the PDF text ('делились подоб-/ного'), hence quote_verbatim=false. English translation: 'one in three respondents (32%) believed fakes over the past year, and another quarter (23%) shared this kind of information.'

estimates.measure_type: % of respondents naming social networks as where they most often encountered fake news in the past year
estimates.denominator: 1,000 residents aged 18+ of the Republic of Mordovia, Russia (quota sample); multiple-response question
estimates.definition: Respondent named this channel in answer to a direct question about where they most often came across made-up, fake news over the past year
estimates.misinfo_def: выдуманная или недостоверная информация... чтобы ввести аудиторию в заблуждение [invented or unreliable information ... to mislead the audience]
estimates.source_quote: Прямой вопрос о том, где опрошенные чаще всего за последний год сталкивались в выдуманными, фейковыми новостями, показывает, что основным каналом их распространения являются социальные сети (58 %).
estimates.moderator_quote: Важно отметить, что вопрос о доверии и недоверии задавался всем респондентам без исключения [the author notes that the parallel source questions were asked of all respondents without exception]
estimates.notes: Channel-attribution question (which channel did you most often meet fake news in), so this is a channel-specific recall-exposure share, not an independent prevalence estimate; percentages across channels sum to >100, i.e. multiple response. Denominator is taken to be all 1,000 respondents (the paper does not restrict it to those who reported any exposure). Source quote is de-hyphenated across a line break ('стал-/кивались'), hence quote_verbatim=false. English translation: 'A direct question about where respondents most often came across made-up, fake news over the past year shows that the main channel of their dissemination is social networks (58%).'

estimates.measure_type: % of respondents who heard fake news from friends, acquaintances or relatives in the past year
estimates.value_raw: только лишь каждый десятый опрошенный (10 %) [only one in ten respondents (10%)]; Table 5 rank 5
estimates.denominator: 1,000 residents aged 18+ of the Republic of Mordovia, Russia (quota sample); multiple-response question
estimates.definition: Respondent named friends/acquaintances/relatives when asked where they most often came across made-up, fake news over the past year
estimates.misinfo_def: выдуманная или недостоверная информация... чтобы ввести аудиторию в заблуждение
estimates.source_quote: Обращает на себя внимание, что только лишь каждый десятый опрошенный (10 %) слышал фейковые новости от друзей, знакомых, родственников.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Respondent self-report; the author argues this is depressed by a prior positive disposition towards one's close circle
estimates.moderator_quote: Вероятная причина не столько в том, что в действительности они не являются носителями фейков [The probable reason is not so much that they are not in fact carriers of fakes]
estimates.notes: Same multiple-response channel question. Source quote is de-hyphenated across a line break ('опро-/шенный'), hence quote_verbatim=false. English translation: 'It is notable that only one in ten respondents (10%) heard fake news from friends, acquaintances or relatives.'

missed_or_uncertain: (1) Not extracted: 32% who said they believed fakes in the past year - belief is excluded by protocol. (2) Not extracted: 41% who think fake/unreliable information is noticeably RARER in the sources they normally use, vs 23% who hold the opposite view and 35% who could not say. This is a comparative perception of one's own information environment rather than a perceived amount (a lot/some/none), so I left it out; an adjudicator may reasonably want the 23% ('more fake information where I get my news') as a perceived-environment RECALL row. Note the numerical coincidence with the 23% sharing row - they are different questions. (3) Not extracted: Table 5's three remaining channels (printed newspapers 7%, radio 2%, printed magazines 2%) - table cells only, kept out to avoid inflating the row count from one multiple-response question; they are verbatim and could be added. (4) Not extracted: 75% ('most of those who came across fake news did not notice the catch and were ready to pass them on to their close circle') - a derived ratio whose denominator is not stated, disallowed by R8. (5) Not extracted: fact-checking habits (16% always verify before sharing, 34% when possible, 24% sometimes, 9% never) - behaviour towards news in general, not a misinformation share. (6) Not extracted: source-use ranking (TV 63%, internet publications 63%, social networks 62%...) and trust/distrust table - media diet and trust, not misinformation prevalence. (7) The abstract ('three out of ten') contradicts the Results ('every second (51%)') for the frequency headline; adjudicator should be aware both numbers appear in the same paper.

rob.design: Author-run quota (non-probability) survey of 1,000 residents of the Republic of Mordovia, Russia, fielded April-May 2023 across 22 municipal districts and the city of Saransk (>80 settlements); quotas on sex, age and settlement type (Table 1); mostly self-completion online via Google Forms, with face-to-face interviews for older/offline respondents; analysed in IBM SPSS Statistics 26 using descriptive statistics, multivariate distributions and some correlations. No response rate is reported. The author states the sampling error is 'analytical' because the approach is non-random, and cites 3.5% at 95% confidence as the error a comparable probability sample would have. No coder reliability applies (self-report).
rob.item6_quote: Для последующего анализа определим фейковые новости как выдуманную или недостоверную информацию, преднамеренно распространяемую заинтересованными сторонами для того, чтобы ввести аудиторию в заблуждение. [For the following analysis we define fake news as invented or unreliable information deliberately disseminated by interested parties in order to mislead the audience.]
rob.item10_quote: Каждый второй (51 %) сталкивался с ними не менее нескольких раз в месяц, в том числе 15 % – практически ежедневно (табл. 4). [Every second respondent (51%) came across them at least several times a month, including 15% almost daily (Table 4).]
